newsitem.title: CHINA: Siemens eyes China generating market.
newsitem.headline: Siemens eyes China generating market.

text.p: Germany's Siemens AG has launched a drive to win a large slice of a major expansion program by China's strapped power generating industry, the Xinhua news agency said on Thursday.
China will be able to meet only 80 per cent of its equipment needs from domestic sources, paving the way for the other 20 percent to come from overseas companies, Xinhua said.
Siemens has announced it aims to win 20 percent of the market for the supply of generating equipment for power plants in China from overseas companies, it said.
The move will help Siemens' Power Generation Group (KWU), to win 1.0 billion marks in sales in China by the turn of the century, it quoted Dietrich Stahl, vice president of Siemens China, as saying.

Siemens/KWU will invest $100 million to join Dongfang Electric Corporation in southwestern Sichuan province in setting up of joint ventures to construct power plants and make turbines and generators, Stahl said.
It will help to upgrade 15 turbogenerators in the 200 megawatt class at power plants in the northeast, he said.
China's total installed capacity is expected to rise from the current 200 gigawatts to 300 gigawatts by 2000, with an annual increase in 1996-2000 of up to 18,000 megawatts, Xinhua said.
A majority of the capacity growth will be met by domestic equipment, leaving 15-20 percent of China's power plant equipment market for overseas suppliers, it said.
With extensive coal reserves, China will give priority to construction of coal-fuelled plants, encouraging Siemens/KWU to increase investments in steam power plants, Xinhua said.
Siemens/KWU has been involved in construction of five of China's coal-fuelled plants, providing a total capacity of 5,000 megawatts of generating units.
China will have a growing equipment market for its increasing gas turbine and combined-cycle power plants, which are mostly in the south, Xinhua said.
Siemens/KWU will help to expand the southern Guangzhou pumped-storage power plant, China's largest of its kind and one of the largest in the world, Stahl said.
